rules.permitted_development: A two-storey extension may stay within permitted development in England, but the route is tight: the addition normally has to be to the rear, keep within the 3m depth limit and clear the rear-boundary distance test.

rules.height_rules: A two-storey extension should remain clearly subordinate to the host house, staying below the highest roof point and at or below the existing eaves.
rules.depth_rules: A two-storey rear extension should usually project no more than 3m beyond the original rear wall if it is to stay within PD. Once depth, width or side projection increases beyond that, permission is normally needed.
rules.boundary_rules: Once a first floor is added, the boundary test becomes much harder. Rear separation, window position and the effect on neighbouring rooms and gardens all matter.
rules.roof_rules: The roof pitch should, so far as practicable, match the existing house and the extension should stay clearly behind the principal elevation. Bulky side roofs and forward projection are common reasons permission is needed.
